M1.reason: From the side views the outline reads as a long gun with a pump, a receiver and a stock, as the brief asks. The front and back views and the in-hand view are squat blocks, though, and the barrel does not show as a slim tube. The in-hand view shows a wide wooden block at the top with no clear taper from barrel to stock. Right to the brief's words in the side views only.

M2.reason: Measured length 28.8 against the brief's 30 (4% off), so within the 15% band. The width (15.2) and height (2.7) are the measured values and are not checked against the brief.

M3.reason: Present: the wooden pump (mid-length, below the receiver in the below and top views), the wooden stock at the rear, the black receiver and a box on the side that reads as a trigger guard. Not clear: the barrel is a squarish section in the front view and does not read as round, and the trigger and the front sight are not distinct in any view. A round part with the wrong number of sides caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: Black metal on the receiver and barrel, dark-brown wood on the pump and stock, as the brief says. The colour and material split matches the brief's words in every view.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no surface detail. The wood grain on the pump and stock and the mottling on the metal are plausible wear and add nothing the brief rules out. The brown mottling on the receiver in the first-person view reads as rust, a little beyond 'black metal', but not enough to call wrong.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, as set out in the rubric (measured apart). The line-up result given is that judges picked D, not A, in four orders, so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The w_ model lies along its length as a dropped gun should. The muzzle points right in the left view and left in the right view, so the mirror is consistent. Its origin is not visible in the pictures, but nothing in the pictures is off.

M8.reason: SMAK checks are clean (checkErrors empty). 204 triangles is under twice the median of 138 (276), and under the 291 that Valve's most of this kind spends. Nothing open that a player sees: the side box on the receiver reads solid in first-person.png and TOP.

W1.reason: In the attack frames the wooden block stays with the hand from frame 0 to 20 and does not part from it. In the first-person still, though, the weapon's block rises straight up from the hand, where the game's own rises up and to the right, so it is not held the way the original is. In several frames the weapon is cut off by the picture's edge, which does not count against it on its own.
